Modern-day Indore was established on the banks of the [Kanh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanh_River "Kanh River") and [Saraswati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saraswati_River_(Madhya_Pradesh) "Saraswati River (Madhya Pradesh)") rivers and traces its roots to its 16th-century founding as a trading hub between the [Deccan Plateau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deccan_Plateau "Deccan Plateau") and [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-12) Following the conquest of [Malwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa "Malwa") by [Peshwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshwa "Peshwa")[Baji Rao I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baji_Rao_I "Baji Rao I"), the city came under the control of the [Maratha Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Confederacy "Maratha Confederacy") until its annexation by the [British East India Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_East_India_Company "British East India Company").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-14) Prior to [Indian independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_independence_movement "Indian independence movement"), [the Kingdom of Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore_State "Indore State") was a nineteen [Gun Salute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salute_state "Salute state")[Princely State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princely_State "Princely State") of the [British Raj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj") with the [Holkars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Holkar "House of Holkar") as rulers.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-15)

With an estimated population of 5.6 million in 2025 distributed over nearly 10 thousand square kilometres, the metropolitan region encompassing Indore, [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain "Ujjain"), [Dewas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewas "Dewas"), [Pithampur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pithampur "Pithampur") and [Nagda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagda "Nagda") serves as the financial capital of Madhya Pradesh. One of India's main industrial hubs, the metropolitan region is a major center for pharmaceutical and automotive manufacturing with, notably, [Asia’s longest test track](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NATRAX "NATRAX").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-:6-20)

The largest education hub in central India, it is home to an [Indian Institute of Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Technology_Indore "Indian Institute of Technology Indore") and an [Indian Institute of Management](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Institute_of_Management_Indore "Indian Institute of Management Indore") and is one of the cities selected under the [central government's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_India "Government of India") flagship [Smart Cities Mission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_Cities_Mission "Smart Cities Mission") and [Swachh Survekshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swachh_Survekshan "Swachh Survekshan") programmes.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-24)
Consistently ranked as India's [cleanest city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cleanest_cities_in_India "List of cleanest cities in India"), Indore is regularly commended for its clean air and proper waste management.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-30)

## Etymology
[Gupta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gupta_Empire "Gupta Empire") inscriptions name Indore as "Indrapura".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-auto1-31) It is believed that the city is named after its Indreshwar Mahadev Temple, where [Shiva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shiva "Shiva") is the presiding deity.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-33) It is believed that [Indra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indra "Indra") himself did _[Tapasya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tapas\_(Indian\_religions) "Tapas (Indian religions)")_ (meditation) in this place and led sage Swami Indrapuri to establish the temple. Later, [Tukoji Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tukoji_Rao_Holkar "Tukoji Rao Holkar") who belonged to the Holkar clan of the Marathas and was the feudatory of Indore, renovated the temple.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-34) The older name of Indore is believed to be **Indur**, as referenced in historical records.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-35) In 2017, a proposal was brought forward by the Indore Municipal Corporation to rename the city as "Indur".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-37)

## History
### Gupta Empire (Gupta era)
[Gupta Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gupta_Empire "Gupta Empire") inscription mentions Indore as city/town of Indrapura in Gupta Indore Copper plate inscription dated 146 Gupta era or 465 CE.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-38) These are also some of the earliest mentions of Indore where the city is mentioned as 'Indrapura'.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-39) Indrapura (modern day Indore) was then known for its sun temple, where in 464–65 CE, Gupta king [Skandagupta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skandagupta "Skandagupta") had made an endowment for the permanent maintenance of the city's sun temple. The temple was constructed by two merchants of the city – Achalavarman and Bhṛikuṇṭhasiṁha.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-auto1-31)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-40)
[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/466_CE_Indore_Copper_Plate_Inscription%2C_Hinduism%2C_Skandagupta%2C_Sanskrit.jpg/250px-466_CE_Indore_Copper_Plate_Inscription%2C_Hinduism%2C_Skandagupta%2C_Sanskrit.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:466_CE_Indore_Copper_Plate_Inscription,_Hinduism,_Skandagupta,_Sanskrit.jpg)
An early Gupta era inscription from ancient India. This is a photograph of a personal copy of plates published by John Fleet in 1888, with Inscriptions of the Early Gupta Kings And Their Successors, as a part of the Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum series, Vol. 3

## History
### Holkar era (Maratha Empire)
During the [Mughal era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mughal_Empire "Mughal Empire"), the area under the modern Indore district was equally divided between the administrations (_[sarkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarkar\_(administrative\_division) "Sarkar (administrative division)")_ s) of [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain "Ujjain") and [Mandu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandu,_Madhya_Pradesh "Mandu, Madhya Pradesh"). Kampel was the headquarters of a _mahal_ (administrative unit) under the Ujjain _sarkar_ of [Malwa Subah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa_Subah "Malwa Subah") (province). The area of the modern Indore city was included in the [Kampel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampel,_Indore "Kampel, Indore")[pargana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pargana "Pargana") (administrative unit).[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-gazetteer_1971-41)

## History
### Holkar era (Maratha Empire)
In 1715, the [Marathas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire "Maratha Empire") invaded this region (Mughal territory) and demanded [chauth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chauth "Chauth") (tax) from the Mughal _Amil_ (administrator) of Kampel. The Amil fled to [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain "Ujjain"), and the local [zamindars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zamindar "Zamindar") agreed to pay Chauth to the Marathas. The chief zamindar, [Nandlal Chaudhary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rao_Nandlal_Chaudhary "Rao Nandlal Chaudhary") (later known as Nandlal Mandloi), paid a chauth of around Rs. 25,000 to the Marathas. [Jai Singh II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jai_Singh_II "Jai Singh II"), the Mughal Governor of Malwa, reached Kampel on 8 May 1715, and defeated the Marathas in a battle near the village. The Marathas came back in early 1716, and raided Kampel in 1717. In March 1718, the Marathas, led by [Santaji Bhonsale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhonsle_(clan) "Bhonsle (clan)"), invaded Malwa again, but were unsuccessful this time.

## History
### Holkar era (Maratha Empire)
By 1720, the headquarters of the local pargana were transferred from Kampel to Indore, due to the increasing commercial activity in the city. In 1724, the Marathas under the new [Peshwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshwa "Peshwa")[Baji Rao I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baji_Rao_I "Baji Rao I"), launched a fresh attack on the Mughals in Malwa. Baji Rao I himself led the campaign, accompanied by his lieutenants [Udaji Rao Pawar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhar_State "Dhar State"), [Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") and [Ranoji Scindia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranoji_Scindia "Ranoji Scindia"). The Mughal [Nizam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qamar-ud-din_Khan,_Asaf_Jah_I "Qamar-ud-din Khan, Asaf Jah I") met the [Peshwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshwa "Peshwa") at [Nalchha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nalchha "Nalchha") on 18 May 1724, and acceded to his demand of collecting chauth from the area. The Peshwa returned to the [Deccan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deccan "Deccan"), but left [Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") at Indore to oversee the chauth collection.

## History
### Holkar era (Maratha Empire)
The Marathas maintained friendly relations with Nandlal Chaudhary, who held influence over the local [Sardars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sardar "Sardar") (chiefs). In 1728, they defeated the Mughals decisively in the battle of [Amjhera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battles_involving_the_Maratha_Empire "Battles involving the Maratha Empire"), and consolidated their authority in the area over the next few years. On 3 October 1730, [Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") was appointed as the Maratha chief of [Malwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa "Malwa"). The local zamindars, who had the title of [Chaudhari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chowdhury "Chowdhury"), came to be known as _Mandloi_ s (after [mandal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehsil "Tehsil"), an administrative unit) during the [Maratha reign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire "Maratha Empire"). The [Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Holkar "House of Holkar") dynasty of the Marathas, which controlled the region, conferred the title of _Rao_ upon the local zamindar family.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-42) After Nandlal died, his son Tejkarana was accepted as the _Mandloi_ of Kampel by the [Peshwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshwa "Peshwa")[Baji Rao I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baji_Rao_I "Baji Rao I"). The pargana was formally granted to [Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") by merging 28 and one-half Pargana by the Peshwa in 1733. The pargana headquarters were transferred back to Kampel during his reign.

## History
### Holkar era (Maratha Empire)
After his death, his daughter-in-law [Ahilyabai Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahilyabai_Holkar "Ahilyabai Holkar") moved the headquarters to Indore in 1766. The [tehsil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehsil "Tehsil") of Kampel was converted into Indore tehsil by a change in the name.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-gazetteer_1971-41) Ahilyabai Holkar moved the state's capital to [Maheshwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maheshwar "Maheshwar") in 1767, but Indore remained an important commercial and military centre.

**Ujjain** (, Hindi pronunciation:[[ʊ̯d͡ːʑæn]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/c/c1/Ujjain.ogg/Ujjain.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ujjain.ogg "File:Ujjain.ogg"), [[əʋən̪t̪ɪkaː]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu")), also known as **Ujjayini**, is a city in [Ujjain district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_district "Ujjain district") of the [Indian state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_and_territories_of_India "States and territories of India") of [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh"). It is the fifth-largest city in Madhya Pradesh by population and is the [administrative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_administration "Public administration") as well as religious centre of Ujjain district and [Ujjain division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_division "Ujjain division").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-census-3) It is one of the Hindu pilgrimage centres of [Sapta Puri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sapta_Puri "Sapta Puri") famous for the _[Kumbh Mela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumbh\_Mela "Kumbh Mela")_[(Simhastha)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_Simhastha "Ujjain Simhastha") held there every 12 years.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-Simhasth-5) The ancient and world famous temple of [Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahakaleshwar_Jyotirlinga "Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga") is located in the center of the city.

The city has been one of the most prominent trade and political centres of the [Indian subcontinent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_subcontinent "Indian subcontinent") from the time of the ancient [Mahājanapadas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahajanapadas "Mahajanapadas") until the British colonisation of India.

An ancient city situated on the eastern bank of the [Shipra River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shipra_River "Shipra River"), then known as **Avantika,**[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-6) it was the most prominent city on the [Malwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa "Malwa") plateau of [central India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_India "Central India") for much of its history. It emerged as the political centre of central India around 600 BCE. It was the capital of the ancient [Avanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avanti_(India) "Avanti (India)") kingdom, one of the sixteen Mahājanapadas. During the 18th century, the city briefly became the capital of the [Scindia state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scindia_Dynasty "Scindia Dynasty") of the [Maratha Confederacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Confederacy "Maratha Confederacy"), when [Ranoji Scindia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranoji_Scindia "Ranoji Scindia") established his capital at Ujjain in 1731. It remained an important political, commercial, and cultural centre of [Central India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_India "Central India") until the early 19th century, when the [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj") administrators decided to develop [Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore "Indore") as an alternative to it. Ujjain continues to be an important place of pilgrimage for [Shaivites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaivism "Shaivism"), [Vaishnavites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaishnavism "Vaishnavism") and [Shaktas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaktism "Shaktism").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-sahaja-8) Bathing in the holy Shipra river of Ujjain liberates one from sins. Therefore, Ujjain is also called the 'Mokshadayini city'.

The name of this river is taken among the holy rivers like [Kaveri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaveri "Kaveri"), [Narmada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narmada_River "Narmada River"), [Godavari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Godavari_River "Godavari River") and [Krishna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_River "Krishna River").
According to Puranic legend, Ujjain, along with [Haridwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haridwar "Haridwar"), [Nashik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashik "Nashik"), and [Prayag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allahabad "Allahabad"), is one of four sites where drops of _[amrita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amrita "Amrita")_,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-9) the elixir of immortality, accidentally spilled over from a _[kumbha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumbha "Kumbha")_ (pitcher) while being carried by the celestial bird [Garuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garuda "Garuda") during the _[Samudra Manthana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samudra\_manthan "Samudra manthan")_, or the churning of the ocean of milk.
Ujjain has been selected as one of the hundred Indian cities to be developed as a [smart city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_city "Smart city") under Prime Minister [Narendra Modi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narendra_Modi "Narendra Modi")'s flagship [Smart Cities Mission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_Cities_Mission "Smart Cities Mission").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-10)

## History
### Prehistoric era
Excavations at [Kayatha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaytha "Kaytha") (around 26 km from Ujjain) have revealed [Chalcolithic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chalcolithic "Chalcolithic") agricultural settlements dating to around 2000 BCE.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-PKB_2012-11) Chalcolithic sites have also been discovered at other areas around Ujjain, including [Nagda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagda "Nagda"), but excavations at Ujjain itself have not revealed any Chalcolithic settlements. Archaeologist [H. D. Sankalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasmukh_Dhirajlal_Sankalia "Hasmukh Dhirajlal Sankalia") theorised that the Chalcolithic settlements at Ujjain were probably destroyed by the [Iron Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Age "Iron Age") settlers.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPranab_Kumar_Bhattacharyya19771%E2%80%932-12)
According to [Hermann Kulke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Kulke "Hermann Kulke") and [Dietmar Rothermund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dietmar_Rothermund "Dietmar Rothermund"), [Avanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avanti_(India) "Avanti (India)"), whose capital was Ujjain, "was one of the earliest outposts in central India" and showed signs of early incipient urbanisation around 700 BCE.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-13) Around 600 BCE, Ujjain emerged as the political, commercial, and cultural centre of [Malwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa "Malwa") plateau.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-Trudy_2012-14)

## Government and jurisdiction
Most of the regions surrounding the city are administered by the [Ujjain Municipal Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_Municipal_Corporation "Ujjain Municipal Corporation") (UMC). The city is administered by a Divisional Commissioner and a Collectorate Office as well as the Mayor. They are responsible for the town and Country Planning Department, Forest Department, Public Health Engineering, Public Works Department and MP Electricity Board.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-ujjain-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-indiatimes-54)
Ujjain has been a metropolitan municipality with a mayor-council form of government. The Ujjain Municipal Corporation (UMC) was established in 1956 under the Madhya Pradesh Nagar Palika Nigam Adhiniyam. The UMC was established in 1886 as Nagar Palika, but the Municipal Corporation of Ujjain was declared on a par with the Gwalior Municipal Corporation. The UMC is responsible for public education, correctional institutions, libraries, public safety, recreational facilities, sanitation, water supply, local planning and welfare services. The mayor and councillors are elected to five-year terms.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-ujjain2-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-ujjain3-56)
The [Ujjain Development Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_Development_Authority "Ujjain Development Authority"), also known as UDA, is the urban planning agency serving Ujjain. Its headquarters are located in the Bharatpuri area of Ujjain. It was established under the Madhya Pradesh Town and Country Planning Act, 1973.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-glance-57)

## Government and jurisdiction
[Ujjain Lok Sabha constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Ujjain (Lok Sabha constituency)") is one of the 29 [Lok Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lok_Sabha "Lok Sabha") constituencies in [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh") state in central India. This constituency came into existence in 1951 as one of the 9 LokSabha constituencies in the erstwhile [Madhya Bharat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Bharat "Madhya Bharat") state. It is reserved for the candidates belonging to the [Scheduled Castes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalit "Dalit") since 1966. This constituency covers the entire [Ujjain district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_district "Ujjain district") and part of [Ratlam district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratlam_district "Ratlam district"). Previously, Dr. [Chintamani Malviya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chintamani_Malviya "Chintamani Malviya") of the [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party") was the member of parliament who won in the [2014 Indian general elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_general_elections "2014 Indian general elections").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-58)
The current Member of Parliament from [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Ujjain (Lok Sabha constituency)") is Anil Firojiya ([BJP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party")) after the [Lok Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lok_Sabha "Lok Sabha") Election of 2019.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-59)

## Industry
Major industrial areas surrounding Ujjain are [Dewas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewas "Dewas") Road Industrial Area, Maxi Road Industrial Area Vikram Udhogpuri, and Tajpur Industrial Area.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-62)
[Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore "Indore") and [Dewas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewas "Dewas") are the cities where majority of the industries are present. Both Indore and Dewas are in close proximity to Ujjain, providing employment to people in Ujjain and nearby areas.
The [Government of Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Madhya_Pradesh "Government of Madhya Pradesh") has allotted 1,200 acres for the development of an industrial area on the Dewas-Ujjain Road (MP State Highway 18) near Narwar village. Originally named "Vikramaditya Knowledge City", the area was envisaged as an educational hub. Due to diminished investment prospects, it was renamed to "[Vikram Udyog Nagari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vikram_Udyog_Nagari "Vikram Udyog Nagari")" ("Vikram Industrial City"). As of 2014, the government has conceptualised it as a half-industrial, half-educational area. The stakeholders in the project include the state government and the [Delhi Mumbai Industrial Corridor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi_Mumbai_Industrial_Corridor?action=edit&redlink=1 "Delhi Mumbai Industrial Corridor (page does not exist)") (DMIC) Trust.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-63)

## Transportation
### Airport
Ujjain does not have any airport but has an [airstrip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_Airstrip "Ujjain Airstrip") on Dewas road which is used for air transport purposes. In 2013, the [Government of Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Madhya_Pradesh "Government of Madhya Pradesh") started a Ujjain-Bhopal air services as a joint venture with [Ventura AirConnect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventura_AirConnect "Ventura AirConnect"). Due to very low booking, the ambitious project was scrapped. The main reason for the failure of the plan was due to improper timing of flights. The nearest airport is the [Devi Ahilyabai Holkar International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devi_Ahilyabai_Holkar_International_Airport "Devi Ahilyabai Holkar International Airport") at [Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore "Indore") (57 km).

## Etymology
[Gupta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gupta_Empire "Gupta Empire") inscriptions name Indore as "Indrapura".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-auto1-31) It is believed that the city is named after its Indreshwar Mahadev Temple, where [Shiva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shiva "Shiva") is the presiding deity.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-33) It is believed that [Indra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indra "Indra") himself did _[Tapasya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tapas\_(Indian\_religions) "Tapas (Indian religions)")_ (meditation) in this place and led sage Swami Indrapuri to establish the temple. Later, [Tukoji Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tukoji_Rao_Holkar "Tukoji Rao Holkar") who belonged to the Holkar clan of the Marathas and was the feudatory of Indore, renovated the temple.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-34) The older name of Indore is believed to be **Indur**, as referenced in historical records.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-35) In 2017, a proposal was brought forward by the Indore Municipal Corporation to rename the city as "Indur".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-37)

## History
### Gupta Empire (Gupta era)
[Gupta Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gupta_Empire "Gupta Empire") inscription mentions Indore as city/town of Indrapura in Gupta Indore Copper plate inscription dated 146 Gupta era or 465 CE.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-38) These are also some of the earliest mentions of Indore where the city is mentioned as 'Indrapura'.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-39) Indrapura (modern day Indore) was then known for its sun temple, where in 464–65 CE, Gupta king [Skandagupta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skandagupta "Skandagupta") had made an endowment for the permanent maintenance of the city's sun temple. The temple was constructed by two merchants of the city – Achalavarman and Bhṛikuṇṭhasiṁha.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-auto1-31)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-40)

## History
### Holkar era (Maratha Empire)
During the [Mughal era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mughal_Empire "Mughal Empire"), the area under the modern Indore district was equally divided between the administrations (_[sarkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarkar\_(administrative\_division) "Sarkar (administrative division)")_ s) of [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain "Ujjain") and [Mandu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandu,_Madhya_Pradesh "Mandu, Madhya Pradesh"). Kampel was the headquarters of a _mahal_ (administrative unit) under the Ujjain _sarkar_ of [Malwa Subah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa_Subah "Malwa Subah") (province). The area of the modern Indore city was included in the [Kampel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampel,_Indore "Kampel, Indore")[pargana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pargana "Pargana") (administrative unit).[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-gazetteer_1971-41)
texts.14:
## History
### Holkar era (Maratha Empire)
In 1715, the [Marathas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire "Maratha Empire") invaded this region (Mughal territory) and demanded [chauth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chauth "Chauth") (tax) from the Mughal _Amil_ (administrator) of Kampel. The Amil fled to [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain "Ujjain"), and the local [zamindars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zamindar "Zamindar") agreed to pay Chauth to the Marathas. The chief zamindar, [Nandlal Chaudhary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rao_Nandlal_Chaudhary "Rao Nandlal Chaudhary") (later known as Nandlal Mandloi), paid a chauth of around Rs. 25,000 to the Marathas. [Jai Singh II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jai_Singh_II "Jai Singh II"), the Mughal Governor of Malwa, reached Kampel on 8 May 1715, and defeated the Marathas in a battle near the village. The Marathas came back in early 1716, and raided Kampel in 1717. In March 1718, the Marathas, led by [Santaji Bhonsale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhonsle_(clan) "Bhonsle (clan)"), invaded Malwa again, but were unsuccessful this time.
texts.15:
## History
### Holkar era (Maratha Empire)
By 1720, the headquarters of the local pargana were transferred from Kampel to Indore, due to the increasing commercial activity in the city. In 1724, the Marathas under the new [Peshwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshwa "Peshwa")[Baji Rao I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baji_Rao_I "Baji Rao I"), launched a fresh attack on the Mughals in Malwa. Baji Rao I himself led the campaign, accompanied by his lieutenants [Udaji Rao Pawar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhar_State "Dhar State"), [Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") and [Ranoji Scindia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranoji_Scindia "Ranoji Scindia"). The Mughal [Nizam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qamar-ud-din_Khan,_Asaf_Jah_I "Qamar-ud-din Khan, Asaf Jah I") met the [Peshwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshwa "Peshwa") at [Nalchha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nalchha "Nalchha") on 18 May 1724, and acceded to his demand of collecting chauth from the area. The Peshwa returned to the [Deccan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deccan "Deccan"), but left [Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") at Indore to oversee the chauth collection.
texts.16:
## History
### Holkar era (Maratha Empire)
The Marathas maintained friendly relations with Nandlal Chaudhary, who held influence over the local [Sardars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sardar "Sardar") (chiefs). In 1728, they defeated the Mughals decisively in the battle of [Amjhera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battles_involving_the_Maratha_Empire "Battles involving the Maratha Empire"), and consolidated their authority in the area over the next few years. On 3 October 1730, [Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") was appointed as the Maratha chief of [Malwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa "Malwa"). The local zamindars, who had the title of [Chaudhari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chowdhury "Chowdhury"), came to be known as _Mandloi_ s (after [mandal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehsil "Tehsil"), an administrative unit) during the [Maratha reign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Empire "Maratha Empire"). The [Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Holkar "House of Holkar") dynasty of the Marathas, which controlled the region, conferred the title of _Rao_ upon the local zamindar family.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-42) After Nandlal died, his son Tejkarana was accepted as the _Mandloi_ of Kampel by the [Peshwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peshwa "Peshwa")[Baji Rao I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baji_Rao_I "Baji Rao I"). The pargana was formally granted to [Malhar Rao Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malhar_Rao_Holkar "Malhar Rao Holkar") by merging 28 and one-half Pargana by the Peshwa in 1733. The pargana headquarters were transferred back to Kampel during his reign.

## History
### Holkar era (Maratha Empire)
After his death, his daughter-in-law [Ahilyabai Holkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahilyabai_Holkar "Ahilyabai Holkar") moved the headquarters to Indore in 1766. The [tehsil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tehsil "Tehsil") of Kampel was converted into Indore tehsil by a change in the name.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore#cite_note-gazetteer_1971-41) Ahilyabai Holkar moved the state's capital to [Maheshwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maheshwar "Maheshwar") in 1767, but Indore remained an important commercial and military centre.

texts.5: **Ujjain** (, Hindi pronunciation:[[ʊ̯d͡ːʑæn]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/c/c1/Ujjain.ogg/Ujjain.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ujjain.ogg "File:Ujjain.ogg"), [[əʋən̪t̪ɪkaː]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu")), also known as **Ujjayini**, is a city in [Ujjain district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_district "Ujjain district") of the [Indian state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_and_territories_of_India "States and territories of India") of [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh"). It is the fifth-largest city in Madhya Pradesh by population and is the [administrative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_administration "Public administration") as well as religious centre of Ujjain district and [Ujjain division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_division "Ujjain division").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-census-3) It is one of the Hindu pilgrimage centres of [Sapta Puri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sapta_Puri "Sapta Puri") famous for the _[Kumbh Mela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumbh\_Mela "Kumbh Mela")_[(Simhastha)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_Simhastha "Ujjain Simhastha") held there every 12 years.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-Simhasth-5) The ancient and world famous temple of [Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahakaleshwar_Jyotirlinga "Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga") is located in the center of the city.
texts.6: The city has been one of the most prominent trade and political centres of the [Indian subcontinent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_subcontinent "Indian subcontinent") from the time of the ancient [Mahājanapadas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahajanapadas "Mahajanapadas") until the British colonisation of India.
texts.7: An ancient city situated on the eastern bank of the [Shipra River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shipra_River "Shipra River"), then known as **Avantika,**[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-6) it was the most prominent city on the [Malwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa "Malwa") plateau of [central India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_India "Central India") for much of its history. It emerged as the political centre of central India around 600 BCE. It was the capital of the ancient [Avanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avanti_(India) "Avanti (India)") kingdom, one of the sixteen Mahājanapadas. During the 18th century, the city briefly became the capital of the [Scindia state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scindia_Dynasty "Scindia Dynasty") of the [Maratha Confederacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Confederacy "Maratha Confederacy"), when [Ranoji Scindia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranoji_Scindia "Ranoji Scindia") established his capital at Ujjain in 1731. It remained an important political, commercial, and cultural centre of [Central India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_India "Central India") until the early 19th century, when the [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj") administrators decided to develop [Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore "Indore") as an alternative to it. Ujjain continues to be an important place of pilgrimage for [Shaivites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaivism "Shaivism"), [Vaishnavites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaishnavism "Vaishnavism") and [Shaktas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaktism "Shaktism").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-sahaja-8) Bathing in the holy Shipra river of Ujjain liberates one from sins. Therefore, Ujjain is also called the 'Mokshadayini city'.
texts.8:
The name of this river is taken among the holy rivers like [Kaveri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaveri "Kaveri"), [Narmada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narmada_River "Narmada River"), [Godavari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Godavari_River "Godavari River") and [Krishna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_River "Krishna River").
According to Puranic legend, Ujjain, along with [Haridwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haridwar "Haridwar"), [Nashik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashik "Nashik"), and [Prayag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allahabad "Allahabad"), is one of four sites where drops of _[amrita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amrita "Amrita")_,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-9) the elixir of immortality, accidentally spilled over from a _[kumbha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumbha "Kumbha")_ (pitcher) while being carried by the celestial bird [Garuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garuda "Garuda") during the _[Samudra Manthana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samudra\_manthan "Samudra manthan")_, or the churning of the ocean of milk.
Ujjain has been selected as one of the hundred Indian cities to be developed as a [smart city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_city "Smart city") under Prime Minister [Narendra Modi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narendra_Modi "Narendra Modi")'s flagship [Smart Cities Mission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_Cities_Mission "Smart Cities Mission").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-10)

## History
### Prehistoric era
Excavations at [Kayatha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaytha "Kaytha") (around 26 km from Ujjain) have revealed [Chalcolithic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chalcolithic "Chalcolithic") agricultural settlements dating to around 2000 BCE.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-PKB_2012-11) Chalcolithic sites have also been discovered at other areas around Ujjain, including [Nagda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagda "Nagda"), but excavations at Ujjain itself have not revealed any Chalcolithic settlements. Archaeologist [H. D. Sankalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasmukh_Dhirajlal_Sankalia "Hasmukh Dhirajlal Sankalia") theorised that the Chalcolithic settlements at Ujjain were probably destroyed by the [Iron Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Age "Iron Age") settlers.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPranab_Kumar_Bhattacharyya19771%E2%80%932-12)
According to [Hermann Kulke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Kulke "Hermann Kulke") and [Dietmar Rothermund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dietmar_Rothermund "Dietmar Rothermund"), [Avanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avanti_(India) "Avanti (India)"), whose capital was Ujjain, "was one of the earliest outposts in central India" and showed signs of early incipient urbanisation around 700 BCE.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-13) Around 600 BCE, Ujjain emerged as the political, commercial, and cultural centre of [Malwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa "Malwa") plateau.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-Trudy_2012-14)

## Government and jurisdiction
Most of the regions surrounding the city are administered by the [Ujjain Municipal Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_Municipal_Corporation "Ujjain Municipal Corporation") (UMC). The city is administered by a Divisional Commissioner and a Collectorate Office as well as the Mayor. They are responsible for the town and Country Planning Department, Forest Department, Public Health Engineering, Public Works Department and MP Electricity Board.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-ujjain-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-indiatimes-54)
Ujjain has been a metropolitan municipality with a mayor-council form of government. The Ujjain Municipal Corporation (UMC) was established in 1956 under the Madhya Pradesh Nagar Palika Nigam Adhiniyam. The UMC was established in 1886 as Nagar Palika, but the Municipal Corporation of Ujjain was declared on a par with the Gwalior Municipal Corporation. The UMC is responsible for public education, correctional institutions, libraries, public safety, recreational facilities, sanitation, water supply, local planning and welfare services. The mayor and councillors are elected to five-year terms.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-ujjain2-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-ujjain3-56)
The [Ujjain Development Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_Development_Authority "Ujjain Development Authority"), also known as UDA, is the urban planning agency serving Ujjain. Its headquarters are located in the Bharatpuri area of Ujjain. It was established under the Madhya Pradesh Town and Country Planning Act, 1973.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-glance-57)
texts.27:
## Government and jurisdiction
[Ujjain Lok Sabha constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Ujjain (Lok Sabha constituency)") is one of the 29 [Lok Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lok_Sabha "Lok Sabha") constituencies in [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh") state in central India. This constituency came into existence in 1951 as one of the 9 LokSabha constituencies in the erstwhile [Madhya Bharat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Bharat "Madhya Bharat") state. It is reserved for the candidates belonging to the [Scheduled Castes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalit "Dalit") since 1966. This constituency covers the entire [Ujjain district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_district "Ujjain district") and part of [Ratlam district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratlam_district "Ratlam district"). Previously, Dr. [Chintamani Malviya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chintamani_Malviya "Chintamani Malviya") of the [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party") was the member of parliament who won in the [2014 Indian general elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_general_elections "2014 Indian general elections").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-58)
The current Member of Parliament from [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Ujjain (Lok Sabha constituency)") is Anil Firojiya ([BJP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party")) after the [Lok Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lok_Sabha "Lok Sabha") Election of 2019.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-59)

## Industry
Major industrial areas surrounding Ujjain are [Dewas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewas "Dewas") Road Industrial Area, Maxi Road Industrial Area Vikram Udhogpuri, and Tajpur Industrial Area.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-62)
[Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore "Indore") and [Dewas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewas "Dewas") are the cities where majority of the industries are present. Both Indore and Dewas are in close proximity to Ujjain, providing employment to people in Ujjain and nearby areas.
The [Government of Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Madhya_Pradesh "Government of Madhya Pradesh") has allotted 1,200 acres for the development of an industrial area on the Dewas-Ujjain Road (MP State Highway 18) near Narwar village. Originally named "Vikramaditya Knowledge City", the area was envisaged as an educational hub. Due to diminished investment prospects, it was renamed to "[Vikram Udyog Nagari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vikram_Udyog_Nagari "Vikram Udyog Nagari")" ("Vikram Industrial City"). As of 2014, the government has conceptualised it as a half-industrial, half-educational area. The stakeholders in the project include the state government and the [Delhi Mumbai Industrial Corridor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi_Mumbai_Industrial_Corridor?action=edit&redlink=1 "Delhi Mumbai Industrial Corridor (page does not exist)") (DMIC) Trust.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-63)
texts.34:
## Transportation
### Airport
Ujjain does not have any airport but has an [airstrip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_Airstrip "Ujjain Airstrip") on Dewas road which is used for air transport purposes. In 2013, the [Government of Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Madhya_Pradesh "Government of Madhya Pradesh") started a Ujjain-Bhopal air services as a joint venture with [Ventura AirConnect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventura_AirConnect "Ventura AirConnect"). Due to very low booking, the ambitious project was scrapped. The main reason for the failure of the plan was due to improper timing of flights. The nearest airport is the [Devi Ahilyabai Holkar International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devi_Ahilyabai_Holkar_International_Airport "Devi Ahilyabai Holkar International Airport") at [Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore "Indore") (57 km).

**Ujjain** (, Hindi pronunciation:[[ʊ̯d͡ːʑæn]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/c/c1/Ujjain.ogg/Ujjain.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ujjain.ogg "File:Ujjain.ogg"), [[əʋən̪t̪ɪkaː]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu")), also known as **Ujjayini**, is a city in [Ujjain district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_district "Ujjain district") of the [Indian state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_and_territories_of_India "States and territories of India") of [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh"). It is the fifth-largest city in Madhya Pradesh by population and is the [administrative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_administration "Public administration") as well as religious centre of Ujjain district and [Ujjain division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_division "Ujjain division").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-census-3) It is one of the Hindu pilgrimage centres of [Sapta Puri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sapta_Puri "Sapta Puri") famous for the _[Kumbh Mela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumbh\_Mela "Kumbh Mela")_[(Simhastha)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_Simhastha "Ujjain Simhastha") held there every 12 years.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-Simhasth-5) The ancient and world famous temple of [Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahakaleshwar_Jyotirlinga "Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga") is located in the center of the city.

The city has been one of the most prominent trade and political centres of the [Indian subcontinent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_subcontinent "Indian subcontinent") from the time of the ancient [Mahājanapadas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahajanapadas "Mahajanapadas") until the British colonisation of India.

An ancient city situated on the eastern bank of the [Shipra River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shipra_River "Shipra River"), then known as **Avantika,**[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-6) it was the most prominent city on the [Malwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa "Malwa") plateau of [central India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_India "Central India") for much of its history. It emerged as the political centre of central India around 600 BCE. It was the capital of the ancient [Avanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avanti_(India) "Avanti (India)") kingdom, one of the sixteen Mahājanapadas. During the 18th century, the city briefly became the capital of the [Scindia state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scindia_Dynasty "Scindia Dynasty") of the [Maratha Confederacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Confederacy "Maratha Confederacy"), when [Ranoji Scindia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranoji_Scindia "Ranoji Scindia") established his capital at Ujjain in 1731. It remained an important political, commercial, and cultural centre of [Central India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_India "Central India") until the early 19th century, when the [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj") administrators decided to develop [Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore "Indore") as an alternative to it. Ujjain continues to be an important place of pilgrimage for [Shaivites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaivism "Shaivism"), [Vaishnavites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaishnavism "Vaishnavism") and [Shaktas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaktism "Shaktism").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-sahaja-8) Bathing in the holy Shipra river of Ujjain liberates one from sins. Therefore, Ujjain is also called the 'Mokshadayini city'.

The name of this river is taken among the holy rivers like [Kaveri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaveri "Kaveri"), [Narmada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narmada_River "Narmada River"), [Godavari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Godavari_River "Godavari River") and [Krishna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_River "Krishna River").
According to Puranic legend, Ujjain, along with [Haridwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haridwar "Haridwar"), [Nashik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashik "Nashik"), and [Prayag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allahabad "Allahabad"), is one of four sites where drops of _[amrita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amrita "Amrita")_,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-9) the elixir of immortality, accidentally spilled over from a _[kumbha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumbha "Kumbha")_ (pitcher) while being carried by the celestial bird [Garuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garuda "Garuda") during the _[Samudra Manthana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samudra\_manthan "Samudra manthan")_, or the churning of the ocean of milk.
Ujjain has been selected as one of the hundred Indian cities to be developed as a [smart city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_city "Smart city") under Prime Minister [Narendra Modi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narendra_Modi "Narendra Modi")'s flagship [Smart Cities Mission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_Cities_Mission "Smart Cities Mission").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-10)

## History
### Prehistoric era
Excavations at [Kayatha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaytha "Kaytha") (around 26 km from Ujjain) have revealed [Chalcolithic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chalcolithic "Chalcolithic") agricultural settlements dating to around 2000 BCE.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-PKB_2012-11) Chalcolithic sites have also been discovered at other areas around Ujjain, including [Nagda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagda "Nagda"), but excavations at Ujjain itself have not revealed any Chalcolithic settlements. Archaeologist [H. D. Sankalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasmukh_Dhirajlal_Sankalia "Hasmukh Dhirajlal Sankalia") theorised that the Chalcolithic settlements at Ujjain were probably destroyed by the [Iron Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Age "Iron Age") settlers.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPranab_Kumar_Bhattacharyya19771%E2%80%932-12)
According to [Hermann Kulke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Kulke "Hermann Kulke") and [Dietmar Rothermund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dietmar_Rothermund "Dietmar Rothermund"), [Avanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avanti_(India) "Avanti (India)"), whose capital was Ujjain, "was one of the earliest outposts in central India" and showed signs of early incipient urbanisation around 700 BCE.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-13) Around 600 BCE, Ujjain emerged as the political, commercial, and cultural centre of [Malwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa "Malwa") plateau.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-Trudy_2012-14)

## Government and jurisdiction
Most of the regions surrounding the city are administered by the [Ujjain Municipal Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_Municipal_Corporation "Ujjain Municipal Corporation") (UMC). The city is administered by a Divisional Commissioner and a Collectorate Office as well as the Mayor. They are responsible for the town and Country Planning Department, Forest Department, Public Health Engineering, Public Works Department and MP Electricity Board.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-ujjain-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-indiatimes-54)
Ujjain has been a metropolitan municipality with a mayor-council form of government. The Ujjain Municipal Corporation (UMC) was established in 1956 under the Madhya Pradesh Nagar Palika Nigam Adhiniyam. The UMC was established in 1886 as Nagar Palika, but the Municipal Corporation of Ujjain was declared on a par with the Gwalior Municipal Corporation. The UMC is responsible for public education, correctional institutions, libraries, public safety, recreational facilities, sanitation, water supply, local planning and welfare services. The mayor and councillors are elected to five-year terms.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-ujjain2-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-ujjain3-56)
The [Ujjain Development Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_Development_Authority "Ujjain Development Authority"), also known as UDA, is the urban planning agency serving Ujjain. Its headquarters are located in the Bharatpuri area of Ujjain. It was established under the Madhya Pradesh Town and Country Planning Act, 1973.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-glance-57)

## Government and jurisdiction
[Ujjain Lok Sabha constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Ujjain (Lok Sabha constituency)") is one of the 29 [Lok Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lok_Sabha "Lok Sabha") constituencies in [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh") state in central India. This constituency came into existence in 1951 as one of the 9 LokSabha constituencies in the erstwhile [Madhya Bharat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Bharat "Madhya Bharat") state. It is reserved for the candidates belonging to the [Scheduled Castes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalit "Dalit") since 1966. This constituency covers the entire [Ujjain district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_district "Ujjain district") and part of [Ratlam district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratlam_district "Ratlam district"). Previously, Dr. [Chintamani Malviya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chintamani_Malviya "Chintamani Malviya") of the [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party") was the member of parliament who won in the [2014 Indian general elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_general_elections "2014 Indian general elections").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-58)
The current Member of Parliament from [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Ujjain (Lok Sabha constituency)") is Anil Firojiya ([BJP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party")) after the [Lok Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lok_Sabha "Lok Sabha") Election of 2019.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-59)

## Industry
Major industrial areas surrounding Ujjain are [Dewas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewas "Dewas") Road Industrial Area, Maxi Road Industrial Area Vikram Udhogpuri, and Tajpur Industrial Area.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-62)
[Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore "Indore") and [Dewas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewas "Dewas") are the cities where majority of the industries are present. Both Indore and Dewas are in close proximity to Ujjain, providing employment to people in Ujjain and nearby areas.
The [Government of Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Madhya_Pradesh "Government of Madhya Pradesh") has allotted 1,200 acres for the development of an industrial area on the Dewas-Ujjain Road (MP State Highway 18) near Narwar village. Originally named "Vikramaditya Knowledge City", the area was envisaged as an educational hub. Due to diminished investment prospects, it was renamed to "[Vikram Udyog Nagari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vikram_Udyog_Nagari "Vikram Udyog Nagari")" ("Vikram Industrial City"). As of 2014, the government has conceptualised it as a half-industrial, half-educational area. The stakeholders in the project include the state government and the [Delhi Mumbai Industrial Corridor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi_Mumbai_Industrial_Corridor?action=edit&redlink=1 "Delhi Mumbai Industrial Corridor (page does not exist)") (DMIC) Trust.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-63)

## Transportation
### Airport
Ujjain does not have any airport but has an [airstrip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_Airstrip "Ujjain Airstrip") on Dewas road which is used for air transport purposes. In 2013, the [Government of Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Madhya_Pradesh "Government of Madhya Pradesh") started a Ujjain-Bhopal air services as a joint venture with [Ventura AirConnect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventura_AirConnect "Ventura AirConnect"). Due to very low booking, the ambitious project was scrapped. The main reason for the failure of the plan was due to improper timing of flights. The nearest airport is the [Devi Ahilyabai Holkar International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devi_Ahilyabai_Holkar_International_Airport "Devi Ahilyabai Holkar International Airport") at [Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore "Indore") (57 km).

texts.5: **Ujjain** (, Hindi pronunciation:[[ʊ̯d͡ːʑæn]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/c/c1/Ujjain.ogg/Ujjain.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ujjain.ogg "File:Ujjain.ogg"), [[əʋən̪t̪ɪkaː]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu")), also known as **Ujjayini**, is a city in [Ujjain district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_district "Ujjain district") of the [Indian state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/States_and_territories_of_India "States and territories of India") of [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh"). It is the fifth-largest city in Madhya Pradesh by population and is the [administrative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_administration "Public administration") as well as religious centre of Ujjain district and [Ujjain division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_division "Ujjain division").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-census-3) It is one of the Hindu pilgrimage centres of [Sapta Puri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sapta_Puri "Sapta Puri") famous for the _[Kumbh Mela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumbh\_Mela "Kumbh Mela")_[(Simhastha)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_Simhastha "Ujjain Simhastha") held there every 12 years.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-Simhasth-5) The ancient and world famous temple of [Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahakaleshwar_Jyotirlinga "Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga") is located in the center of the city.
texts.6: The city has been one of the most prominent trade and political centres of the [Indian subcontinent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_subcontinent "Indian subcontinent") from the time of the ancient [Mahājanapadas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahajanapadas "Mahajanapadas") until the British colonisation of India.
texts.7: An ancient city situated on the eastern bank of the [Shipra River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shipra_River "Shipra River"), then known as **Avantika,**[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-6) it was the most prominent city on the [Malwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa "Malwa") plateau of [central India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_India "Central India") for much of its history. It emerged as the political centre of central India around 600 BCE. It was the capital of the ancient [Avanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avanti_(India) "Avanti (India)") kingdom, one of the sixteen Mahājanapadas. During the 18th century, the city briefly became the capital of the [Scindia state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scindia_Dynasty "Scindia Dynasty") of the [Maratha Confederacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maratha_Confederacy "Maratha Confederacy"), when [Ranoji Scindia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranoji_Scindia "Ranoji Scindia") established his capital at Ujjain in 1731. It remained an important political, commercial, and cultural centre of [Central India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_India "Central India") until the early 19th century, when the [British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj") administrators decided to develop [Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore "Indore") as an alternative to it. Ujjain continues to be an important place of pilgrimage for [Shaivites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaivism "Shaivism"), [Vaishnavites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaishnavism "Vaishnavism") and [Shaktas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaktism "Shaktism").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-sahaja-8) Bathing in the holy Shipra river of Ujjain liberates one from sins. Therefore, Ujjain is also called the 'Mokshadayini city'.
texts.8:
The name of this river is taken among the holy rivers like [Kaveri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaveri "Kaveri"), [Narmada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narmada_River "Narmada River"), [Godavari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Godavari_River "Godavari River") and [Krishna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna_River "Krishna River").
According to Puranic legend, Ujjain, along with [Haridwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haridwar "Haridwar"), [Nashik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashik "Nashik"), and [Prayag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allahabad "Allahabad"), is one of four sites where drops of _[amrita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amrita "Amrita")_,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-9) the elixir of immortality, accidentally spilled over from a _[kumbha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumbha "Kumbha")_ (pitcher) while being carried by the celestial bird [Garuda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garuda "Garuda") during the _[Samudra Manthana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samudra\_manthan "Samudra manthan")_, or the churning of the ocean of milk.
Ujjain has been selected as one of the hundred Indian cities to be developed as a [smart city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_city "Smart city") under Prime Minister [Narendra Modi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Narendra_Modi "Narendra Modi")'s flagship [Smart Cities Mission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_Cities_Mission "Smart Cities Mission").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-10)

## History
### Prehistoric era
Excavations at [Kayatha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaytha "Kaytha") (around 26 km from Ujjain) have revealed [Chalcolithic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chalcolithic "Chalcolithic") agricultural settlements dating to around 2000 BCE.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-PKB_2012-11) Chalcolithic sites have also been discovered at other areas around Ujjain, including [Nagda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagda "Nagda"), but excavations at Ujjain itself have not revealed any Chalcolithic settlements. Archaeologist [H. D. Sankalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hasmukh_Dhirajlal_Sankalia "Hasmukh Dhirajlal Sankalia") theorised that the Chalcolithic settlements at Ujjain were probably destroyed by the [Iron Age](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Age "Iron Age") settlers.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPranab_Kumar_Bhattacharyya19771%E2%80%932-12)
According to [Hermann Kulke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermann_Kulke "Hermann Kulke") and [Dietmar Rothermund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dietmar_Rothermund "Dietmar Rothermund"), [Avanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avanti_(India) "Avanti (India)"), whose capital was Ujjain, "was one of the earliest outposts in central India" and showed signs of early incipient urbanisation around 700 BCE.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-13) Around 600 BCE, Ujjain emerged as the political, commercial, and cultural centre of [Malwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malwa "Malwa") plateau.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-Trudy_2012-14)

## Government and jurisdiction
Most of the regions surrounding the city are administered by the [Ujjain Municipal Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_Municipal_Corporation "Ujjain Municipal Corporation") (UMC). The city is administered by a Divisional Commissioner and a Collectorate Office as well as the Mayor. They are responsible for the town and Country Planning Department, Forest Department, Public Health Engineering, Public Works Department and MP Electricity Board.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-ujjain-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-indiatimes-54)
Ujjain has been a metropolitan municipality with a mayor-council form of government. The Ujjain Municipal Corporation (UMC) was established in 1956 under the Madhya Pradesh Nagar Palika Nigam Adhiniyam. The UMC was established in 1886 as Nagar Palika, but the Municipal Corporation of Ujjain was declared on a par with the Gwalior Municipal Corporation. The UMC is responsible for public education, correctional institutions, libraries, public safety, recreational facilities, sanitation, water supply, local planning and welfare services. The mayor and councillors are elected to five-year terms.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-ujjain2-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-ujjain3-56)
The [Ujjain Development Authority](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_Development_Authority "Ujjain Development Authority"), also known as UDA, is the urban planning agency serving Ujjain. Its headquarters are located in the Bharatpuri area of Ujjain. It was established under the Madhya Pradesh Town and Country Planning Act, 1973.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-glance-57)

## Government and jurisdiction
[Ujjain Lok Sabha constituency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Ujjain (Lok Sabha constituency)") is one of the 29 [Lok Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lok_Sabha "Lok Sabha") constituencies in [Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Pradesh "Madhya Pradesh") state in central India. This constituency came into existence in 1951 as one of the 9 LokSabha constituencies in the erstwhile [Madhya Bharat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhya_Bharat "Madhya Bharat") state. It is reserved for the candidates belonging to the [Scheduled Castes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalit "Dalit") since 1966. This constituency covers the entire [Ujjain district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_district "Ujjain district") and part of [Ratlam district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratlam_district "Ratlam district"). Previously, Dr. [Chintamani Malviya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chintamani_Malviya "Chintamani Malviya") of the [Bharatiya Janata Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party") was the member of parliament who won in the [2014 Indian general elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_general_elections "2014 Indian general elections").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-58)
The current Member of Parliament from [Ujjain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_(Lok_Sabha_constituency) "Ujjain (Lok Sabha constituency)") is Anil Firojiya ([BJP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatiya_Janata_Party "Bharatiya Janata Party")) after the [Lok Sabha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lok_Sabha "Lok Sabha") Election of 2019.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-59)

## Industry
Major industrial areas surrounding Ujjain are [Dewas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewas "Dewas") Road Industrial Area, Maxi Road Industrial Area Vikram Udhogpuri, and Tajpur Industrial Area.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-62)
[Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore "Indore") and [Dewas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewas "Dewas") are the cities where majority of the industries are present. Both Indore and Dewas are in close proximity to Ujjain, providing employment to people in Ujjain and nearby areas.
The [Government of Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Madhya_Pradesh "Government of Madhya Pradesh") has allotted 1,200 acres for the development of an industrial area on the Dewas-Ujjain Road (MP State Highway 18) near Narwar village. Originally named "Vikramaditya Knowledge City", the area was envisaged as an educational hub. Due to diminished investment prospects, it was renamed to "[Vikram Udyog Nagari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vikram_Udyog_Nagari "Vikram Udyog Nagari")" ("Vikram Industrial City"). As of 2014, the government has conceptualised it as a half-industrial, half-educational area. The stakeholders in the project include the state government and the [Delhi Mumbai Industrial Corridor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi_Mumbai_Industrial_Corridor?action=edit&redlink=1 "Delhi Mumbai Industrial Corridor (page does not exist)") (DMIC) Trust.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain#cite_note-63)

## Transportation
### Airport
Ujjain does not have any airport but has an [airstrip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ujjain_Airstrip "Ujjain Airstrip") on Dewas road which is used for air transport purposes. In 2013, the [Government of Madhya Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Madhya_Pradesh "Government of Madhya Pradesh") started a Ujjain-Bhopal air services as a joint venture with [Ventura AirConnect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventura_AirConnect "Ventura AirConnect"). Due to very low booking, the ambitious project was scrapped. The main reason for the failure of the plan was due to improper timing of flights. The nearest airport is the [Devi Ahilyabai Holkar International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devi_Ahilyabai_Holkar_International_Airport "Devi Ahilyabai Holkar International Airport") at [Indore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indore "Indore") (57 km).

[_Comte_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Count "Count")**Henri Marie Raymond de Toulouse-Lautrec-Montfa**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_de_Toulouse-Lautrec#cite_note-Acte_naissance-1) (24 November 1864– 9 September 1901), known as **Toulouse-Lautrec** (French:[[tuluz lotʁɛk]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/French "Help:IPA/French")), was a French painter, printmaker, draughtsman, caricaturist, and illustrator. His immersion in the colourful and theatrical life of [Paris's Belle Époque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_in_the_Belle_%C3%89poque "Paris in the Belle Époque") in the late 19th century allowed him to produce popular works of art from decadent affairs.

Born into the aristocracy, Toulouse-Lautrec broke both his legs during adolescence, leaving him with a stunted appearance. In later life, he developed an affinity for [brothels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brothel "Brothel") and prostitutes that directed the subject matter for many of his works, which record details of the late-19th-century bohemian lifestyle in Paris. He is among the painters described as [Post-Impressionists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-Impressionism "Post-Impressionism"), with [Paul Cézanne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_C%C3%A9zanne "Paul Cézanne"), [Vincent van Gogh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vincent_van_Gogh "Vincent van Gogh"), [Paul Gauguin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Gauguin "Paul Gauguin"), and [Georges Seurat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georges_Seurat "Georges Seurat") also commonly considered as belonging in this loose group.

Henri Marie Raymond de Toulouse-Lautrec-Montfa[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_de_Toulouse-Lautrec#cite_note-2) was born at Demoiselles d'Imbert du Bosc (his great-aunts) home at rue de l'École Mage (presently 14, rue Henri de Toulouse Lautrec), Albi,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_de_Toulouse-Lautrec#cite_note-Acte_naissance-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_de_Toulouse-Lautrec#cite_note-3) in the south of France, the firstborn child of [Count Alphonse de Toulouse-Lautrec Montfa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Count_Alphonse_de_Toulouse-Lautrec_Montfa "Count Alphonse de Toulouse-Lautrec Montfa") (1838–1913)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_de_Toulouse-Lautrec#cite_note-4) and Adèle Zoë Tapié de Celeyran (1841–1930).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_de_Toulouse-Lautrec#cite_note-5) He was a member of an aristocratic family (descended from both the [Counts of Toulouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Count_of_Toulouse "Count of Toulouse") and [Odet de Foix, Vicomte de Lautrec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odet_of_Foix,_Viscount_of_Lautrec "Odet of Foix, Viscount of Lautrec"), as well as the [Viscounts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viscount "Viscount") of [Montfa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montfa,_Tarn "Montfa, Tarn")). His younger brother was born in 1867 but died the following year.

Both sons enjoyed the [_titres de courtoisie_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Courtesy_title "Courtesy title") of _[Comte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Count "Count")_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_de_Toulouse-Lautrec#cite_note-6) If Toulouse-Lautrec had outlived his father, he would have inherited the family [title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobility_of_France "Nobility of France") of _Comte de Toulouse-Lautrec_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_de_Toulouse-Lautrec#cite_note-7)
After the death of his brother, Toulouse-Lautrec's parents separated, and a nanny cared for him.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_de_Toulouse-Lautrec#cite_note-TL-Book1-8) At the age of eight, Toulouse-Lautrec lived with his mother in Paris, where he drew sketches and caricatures in his exercise workbooks. A friend of his father, [René Princeteau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ren%C3%A9_Princeteau "René Princeteau"), sometimes visited to give informal lessons. Some of Toulouse-Lautrec's early paintings are of horses, a speciality of Princeteau's and a subject Toulouse-Lautrec later revisited in his "Circus Paintings".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_de_Toulouse-Lautrec#cite_note-TL-Book1-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_de_Toulouse-Lautrec#cite_note-9)
In 1875, Toulouse-Lautrec returned to Albi because his mother had concerns about his health. He took thermal baths at [Amélie-les-Bains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Am%C3%A9lie-les-Bains "Amélie-les-Bains"), and his mother consulted doctors in the hope of finding a way to improve her son's growth and development.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_de_Toulouse-Lautrec#cite_note-TL-Book1-8)

### Disability and health problems
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Henri_de_Toulouse-Lautrec&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Disability and health problems")]
[![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/95/Guibert_2.jpg/250px-Guibert_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Guibert_2.jpg)
Mr. Toulouse paints Mr. Lautrec (c.1891), a photomontage by [Maurice Guibert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurice_Guibert "Maurice Guibert")
Toulouse-Lautrec's parents were [first cousins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_cousins "First cousins") (their mothers were sisters),[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_de_Toulouse-Lautrec#cite_note-10) and his [congenital health conditions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congenital_disorder "Congenital disorder") have often been attributed to a family history of [inbreeding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inbreeding "Inbreeding").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_de_Toulouse-Lautrec#cite_note-11)

### Disability and health problems
At the age of 13, Toulouse-Lautrec fractured his right [femur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femur "Femur"), and at age 14, he fractured his left femur.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_de_Toulouse-Lautrec#cite_note-TheTimes-12) The breaks did not heal properly. Modern physicians attribute this to an unknown [genetic disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_disorder "Genetic disorder"), possibly [pycnodysostosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pycnodysostosis "Pycnodysostosis") (sometimes known as 'Toulouse-Lautrec Syndrome'),[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_de_Toulouse-Lautrec#cite_note-Valdes-Socin_2021-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_de_Toulouse-Lautrec#cite_note-Angier-14) or a variant disorder along the lines of [osteopetrosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osteopetrosis "Osteopetrosis"), [achondroplasia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achondroplasia "Achondroplasia"), or [osteogenesis imperfecta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osteogenesis_imperfecta "Osteogenesis imperfecta").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_de_Toulouse-Lautrec#cite_note-15) Toulouse-Lautrec's legs ceased to grow when he reached 1.52 m (5 ft 0 in).[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_de_Toulouse-Lautrec#cite_note-16) He developed an adult torso while retaining his child-sized legs.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henri_de_Toulouse-Lautrec#cite_note-17)

### Disability and health problems
[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f0/1882%2C_Toulouse-Lautrec%2C_The_Marble_Polisher.jpg/250px-1882%2C_Toulouse-Lautrec%2C_The_Marble_Polisher.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:1882,_Toulouse-Lautrec,_The_Marble_Polisher.jpg)
